title: How much does a bookkeeper cost in Nigeria in 2026?
seo_title: How much does a bookkeeper cost in Nigeria? (2026 guide)
description: What outsourced bookkeeping costs in Nigeria in 2026, what drives the price, and what you should get for your money. Clear prices from The Resident Bookkeeper.
answer: In 2026, outsourced bookkeeping for a small Nigerian business usually costs between ₦100,000 a year for a simple AI-assisted service and ₦150,000 to ₦550,000 a month for a fully managed monthly service. The price depends mostly on how many transactions you have each month, how many bank and payment accounts you use, and whether payroll, VAT and stock are included. Old, messy records cost extra to bring up to date first.
body_html:
What decides the price

Bookkeepers price by the amount of work, not by the size of your shop or office. These five things make the biggest difference:

  1. Transactions a month. Every sale, expense and transfer on your statements has to be recorded and matched. A business with 80 transactions a month needs far less time than one with 800.
  2. Number of accounts. Each bank account, POS terminal, card and payment app (Moniepoint, Opay, Paystack and others) needs its own monthly reconciliation.
  3. Payroll. Tracking staff salaries and calculating PAYE adds work every month.
  4. Stock. Shops, pharmacies and manufacturers need cost of sales and stock records.
  5. The state of your records. If your books are months or years behind, they must be brought up to date first. This is called catch-up bookkeeping and is priced separately.

Our prices in Nigeria

These are The Resident Bookkeeper's published prices. The final price is confirmed in writing after a free Books Health Check.

ServicePriceBest for
TRB Books Lite₦100,000 a yearMicro businesses, freelancers, content creators and influencers with up to 100 transactions a month and 2 bank accounts
Essentials₦150,000 a monthUp to 150 transactions a month and 2 bank or card accounts
Growth₦300,000 a monthUp to 400 transactions and 5 accounts, with invoices, bills and payroll records for up to 10 staff

Catch-up₦100,000 per month of recordsBooks that are behind and need to be brought up to date

In-house bookkeeper or outsourced?

A full-time bookkeeper on staff means a monthly salary, pension, leave, equipment and software, and supervision. Many small businesses do not have a full month of bookkeeping work, so they pay for idle time. An outsourced service gives you a team, a reviewer and a fixed fee, and the work continues when someone is on leave.

An in-house bookkeeper makes sense once you have enough daily transactions to keep one person busy, or you need someone in the office for cash handling and stores.

What you should get for the fee

  • Every sale and expense recorded each month
  • Every bank and payment account reconciled, so nothing is missing
  • A monthly profit and loss statement and balance sheet you can read
  • VAT, withholding tax and PAYE tracked as you go, so tax time holds no surprises
  • A written agreement with a clear scope, deadlines and confidentiality terms

Why it pays for itself

Since January 2026, small companies with turnover of ₦100 million or less and fixed assets below ₦250 million pay 0% company income tax under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025. To claim that, you must be able to prove your turnover and assets, and that proof comes from your books. Accurate records also keep you clear of late-filing penalties and help you get loans.

faq.q: Is bookkeeping cheaper than hiring an accountant?
faq.a: Usually, yes. Bookkeeping covers recording and reconciling transactions and producing monthly reports. Filing tax returns, audits and tax advice are separate services, often done by a chartered accountant or tax practitioner who works from the records your bookkeeper keeps.

faq.q: Can I pay for bookkeeping once a year instead of monthly?
faq.a: You can, but it is usually more expensive and less useful. Doing a full year at once is catch-up work, and you miss the monthly reports that help you control cash and plan for tax.

faq.q: Do you charge businesses outside Nigeria in naira?
faq.a: No. We quote in US dollars, British pounds, Canadian dollars and Australian dollars for those countries, and in US dollars for every other country.

title: What records do I need to file company tax in Nigeria?
seo_title: Records you need to file company tax in Nigeria (2026)
description: The documents and records a Nigerian company needs to file its tax returns under the 2026 tax laws, how long to keep them, and how to stay ready all year.
answer: To file company tax in Nigeria you need records that prove your income, expenses, assets and the taxes you have already deducted or paid. That means bank statements for every account, sales invoices, expense receipts, payroll records, a fixed asset list, and receipts for VAT, withholding tax and PAYE, kept up to date in a set of books that produce a profit and loss statement and balance sheet. Company income tax returns are due within six months of your financial year end.
body_html:
The records checklist

Income

  • Bank statements for every business account
  • POS, card and payment-app statements
  • Sales invoices and receipts issued
  • List of customers who owe you

Expenses

  • Supplier invoices, bills and receipts
  • Rent agreement and utility bills
  • List of suppliers you owe
  • Contracts for big or recurring costs

Assets, capital and loans

  • Fixed asset list with purchase dates and costs
  • Receipts for equipment, vehicles and fit-out
  • Loan agreements and repayment schedules
  • Money the owners put in or took out

Staff and taxes

  • Payroll records and payslips
  • PAYE and pension remittance receipts
  • VAT returns and receipts, if registered
  • Withholding tax credit notes received

Why these records matter more since 2026

The Nigeria Tax Act 2025 and the Nigeria Tax Administration Act 2025 took effect on 1 January 2026, and federal taxes are now administered by the Nigeria Revenue Service (NRS). Three changes make good records more important for small businesses:

  1. The small company exemption needs proof. Companies with annual turnover of ₦100 million or less and fixed assets below ₦250 million pay 0% company income tax and are exempt from the 4% development levy. Your books are the evidence that you qualify.
  2. VAT registration depends on turnover. The VAT threshold is ₦50 million a year. You need accurate monthly sales figures to know when you cross it.
  3. Penalties are heavier. Late or missing returns attract fines, and the new law gives the tax authority wider powers to question undocumented transactions.

Key filing dates

TaxWhen it is due
Company income tax returnWithin 6 months of your financial year end
VAT returnBy the 21st of the following month, if registered
Employees' annual income returns (employer)By 31 January for the previous year
PAYE and withholding taxMonthly, to the relevant tax authority

Always confirm current deadlines with the NRS, your State Internal Revenue Service or your tax adviser.

How long to keep records

Keep your books and supporting documents for at least six years. Tax authorities can review earlier years, and you will need the documents to answer their questions. Scanned copies stored safely in the cloud are easier to keep than paper files.

How to stay ready all year

  • Use a separate bank account for the business, and avoid paying business costs from personal accounts
  • Collect statements and receipts every month, not at the end of the year
  • Reconcile every account monthly, so missing or duplicated items are caught early
  • Review a profit and loss statement each month, so the tax bill is never a surprise

faq.q: Do small companies still need to file tax returns if they pay 0% tax?
faq.a: Yes. A small company still files its company income tax return. The 0% rate applies when the return shows turnover and fixed assets within the small company limits.

faq.q: Can I file with only my bank statements?
faq.a: Bank statements are the starting point, but they do not show what each payment was for. You need invoices and receipts to support income and expenses, and a set of books to produce your financial statements.

faq.q: What if my records are already behind?
faq.a: A catch-up service brings past months up to date, starting from your bank statements. It is better to fix the records before filing than to file figures you cannot support.

title: How to calculate PAYE for your staff in Nigeria (2026)
seo_title: How to calculate PAYE in Nigeria in 2026, with a worked example
description: A step-by-step guide to calculating PAYE under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, with the 2026 tax bands, rent relief, deductions and a worked example.
answer: From 1 January 2026, PAYE in Nigeria is worked out on an employee's chargeable income: annual pay minus allowed deductions such as pension contributions and rent relief. The first ₦800,000 a year is tax-free, then rates rise in bands from 15% to 25%. Divide the annual tax by 12 to get the monthly PAYE the employer deducts and remits to the State Internal Revenue Service.
body_html:
The 2026 PAYE tax bands

Chargeable income a yearRate
First ₦800,0000%
Next ₦2,200,00015%
Next ₦9,000,00018%
Next ₦13,000,00021%
Next ₦25,000,00023%
Above ₦50,000,00025%

Employees whose pay is at or below the national minimum wage (₦70,000 a month) pay no PAYE on that employment.

Step by step

  1. Add up annual pay. Basic salary plus allowances (housing, transport and others) for the year.
  2. Take off allowed deductions. These include the employee's pension contribution (8%), NHF where the employee agrees to it, health insurance, life insurance premiums and mortgage interest.
  3. Take off rent relief. 20% of the rent the employee pays in the year, up to ₦500,000, with proof such as a receipt or tenancy agreement. Rent relief replaces the old consolidated relief allowance.
  4. Apply the bands to what is left (the chargeable income).
  5. Divide by 12 for the monthly PAYE to deduct.

Worked example

Amaka earns ₦500,000 a month (₦6,000,000 a year), made up of basic, housing and transport. She pays ₦1,200,000 a year in rent and contributes 8% to her pension.

Annual pay₦6,000,000
Less pension (8%)(₦480,000)
Less rent relief (20% of ₦1,200,000)(₦240,000)
Chargeable income₦5,280,000
First ₦800,000 at 0%₦0
Next ₦2,200,000 at 15%₦330,000
Remaining ₦2,280,000 at 18%₦410,400
Annual PAYE₦740,400
Monthly PAYE₦61,700

Amaka's PAYE is about 12.3% of her gross pay.

What employers must do

  • Register for PAYE with the State Internal Revenue Service where your staff live or work
  • Deduct PAYE every payday and remit it monthly
  • File employees' annual income returns by 31 January for the previous year
  • Keep payroll records, payslips and remittance receipts

The penalties are significant: failing to deduct PAYE can attract a penalty of 40% of the amount not deducted, and late remittance attracts 10% plus interest.

This guide is general information based on the Nigeria Tax Act 2025, not tax advice. Confirm your own figures with your State Internal Revenue Service or tax adviser.

faq.q: Is the first ₦800,000 tax-free for everyone?
faq.a: Yes. Under the 2026 bands, the first ₦800,000 of chargeable income a year is taxed at 0% for every employee.
No. The employee must show proof of rent paid, such as a receipt, tenancy agreement or rent declaration approved by the employer. Relief is 20% of annual rent, up to ₦500,000.

faq.q: Who does PAYE get paid to?
faq.a: PAYE for employees is paid to the State Internal Revenue Service of the state where the employee is resident for tax, not to the federal Nigeria Revenue Service.

title: What is catch-up bookkeeping, and do I need it?
seo_title: What is catch-up bookkeeping? Signs you need it and what it costs
description: Catch-up bookkeeping brings months or years of missing records up to date. Signs you need it, how it works, how long it takes and what it costs.
answer: Catch-up bookkeeping is the work of bringing a business's books up to date when months or years of transactions have not been recorded. A bookkeeper starts from your bank statements, records every sale and expense for the missing period, reconciles each account, and produces a profit and loss statement and balance sheet for each period. You need it if you cannot say what profit you made last year, or you have a tax return, loan application or investor meeting coming up and your records are behind.
body_html:
Signs you need catch-up bookkeeping

  • You have not recorded transactions for three months or more
  • You cannot say what profit you made last year
  • A tax return, tax audit or letter from the tax authority is coming up
  • A bank, investor or buyer has asked for financial statements
  • Business and personal money have been mixed in the same accounts
  • Your previous bookkeeper left and nobody picked up the work

Catch-up or clean-up?

Catch-up fills in periods that were never recorded. Clean-up fixes records that exist but are wrong, such as wrong categories, duplicates, or accounts that do not reconcile. Many businesses need some of both.

How it works

  1. Free review. We look at how far behind you are, how many accounts you have and what records exist.
  2. Checklist and quote. You get a list of what we need and a fixed price based on the months of records.
  3. Collect the records. Bank statements for every account first, then invoices, receipts, payroll and loan documents.
  4. Record and reconcile. Every transaction is recorded and every account reconciled, month by month.
  5. Questions. We send a short list of transactions we cannot identify from the documents.
  6. Reports and review call. You receive the profit and loss statement and balance sheet for each period, and we walk you through them.

How long and how much

A catch-up of up to a year usually takes two to four weeks once all the records arrive. The speed depends mostly on how quickly bank statements and answers come in.

The Resident Bookkeeper charges ₦100,000 per month of records in Nigeria, $199 in the US, £159 in the UK, C$269 in Canada and A$299 in Australia. Businesses in other countries are quoted in US dollars. Clean-up starts from ₦250,000 or $499.

After the catch-up

Once the books are current, keep them that way. A monthly bookkeeping plan means you never face the same backlog again, and you always know where your tax position stands.

faq.q: Can you do catch-up bookkeeping with only bank statements?
faq.a: Yes, bank statements are enough to start. Invoices and receipts make the records more complete, and we tell you which ones matter most.

faq.q: How far back can you go?
faq.a: As far back as you need, usually to the start of the business or the last date your books were up to date.

faq.q: Will catch-up bookkeeping reduce my tax?
faq.a: It makes sure your tax is based on correct figures. Properly recorded expenses and capital often mean the taxable profit is lower than a guess would suggest, and the records let you claim exemptions such as the small company 0% rate where you qualify.
